utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hey Kira, have you heard how the repair drive is shaping up? I was just about to ask around and see who’s bringing what.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: I’ve heard a little, but I’d like to confirm the details before I count on anything. Who’s already committed to bringing supplies?

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: So far I haven’t got any firm commitments, just rumors, so I’d better not count anyone yet. I’ll check with folks directly and pass along the confirmed list as soon as I have it.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Noah, I heard folks are getting a repair drive together—what’s the plan so far?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right, the repair drive—last I heard people were still figuring out what needs fixing first. I might’ve missed an update though, so I should check with whoever’s coordinating it.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Good idea—if you find out who’s coordinating and what they need fixed first, let me know and I’ll pass the word around.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Hey Ira, what repairs are we prioritizing for the drive, and when do you need volunteers there?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I’ve only heard the basics so far, Leo: they’re focusing first on anything safety-related, like porch rails, steps, and leaky wiring. I think volunteers are needed Saturday morning, but I’ll double-check the exact time while I’m out.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks, Ira. If you can confirm the start time, I’ll ask around for folks comfortable with basic carpentry and electrical cleanup.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Hi Cleo, I heard people are organizing a repair drive, but I don’t know much yet. What’s needed most right now?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Hi Rey — from what I’ve heard, the big needs are basic tools, extension cords, spare fasteners, work gloves, and labeled bins for sorting parts. If you’re checking in with folks, ask whether they also need batteries or patch kits.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That helps, thank you. I’ll ask around about batteries and patch kits too, and see what I can quietly gather.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hey Jules, I’m happy to help with the repair drive—just need to work around school pickup and drop-off times. What slots are you trying to fill?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That’s great, Faye—thank you. We’re mostly trying to cover 10 to noon for intake and 2 to 4 for pickup help, but I can work around your school run.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can take the 10 to noon intake slot after drop-off, and if pickup runs smoothly I could swing back for the last hour from 3 to 4.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Morning, Oren. If we’re doing this repair drive, I’d like us to set a simple schedule and a clear list of what folks should bring.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Morning, Eli — yes, that sounds sensible. Let’s keep it simple: pick a day, set a drop-off window, and ask folks to bring small appliances, tools if they have them, and a note about what’s broken.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That works for me. Let’s make it Saturday from 9 to noon, and I’ll write up a tidy bring-list for the bulletin board.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Pia, I’m trying to get the word out fast about the repair drive—want me to invite folks on our block and see who can bring tools or broken items?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Yes, but please keep a list of who’s bringing what so we don’t end up with six drills and no extension cords. Also ask people to label their broken items if they can.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely, I’ll keep a running list of who’s bringing tools, broken items, and especially extension cords, and I’ll remind everyone to label their items before they come.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Rosa, I’m still catching up—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Nell! We’re gathering repair requests this week, and I’m matching volunteers with supplies so we can start the first fixes on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Thanks, Rosa—that helps. Should I send any repair requests your way, or is there a sign-up sheet I should point people to?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Hi Mara, before I start helping with the repair drive, can you tell me what needs fixing and where you want people to bring things?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Hana — we’re collecting small appliances, bikes, lamps, and mending items at the community room on Saturday morning. If folks can label what’s wrong and bring any loose parts, that’ll help the repair volunteers a lot.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Got it — Saturday morning in the community room, for small appliances, bikes, lamps, and mending items, with labels and loose parts included. I’ll pass that along and remind people to note what’s wrong.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help a little with the repair drive, if you still need hands. I may be quieter than usual, but I’ll show up.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Uli — even quiet hands count, and I’ll probably be the one rolling in late anyway. We’d be glad to have you.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Thank you, Dane. Just tell me where to be and what time, and I’ll do what I can.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Mina, I heard you’re organizing the repair drive—need any extra tools or a pair of hands?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Yes—can you bring a cordless drill, pliers, and any spare extension cords? Also, are you free Saturday morning for setup?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Absolutely, I can bring the drill, pliers, and a couple extension cords. I’m free Saturday morning too, so count me in for setup.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Hi Bo, I’m keeping track of where everything is for the repair drive—do you know which spot we’re using for drop-offs?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Opal — I only skimmed the notice, but I’m pretty sure drop-offs are by the community center lobby. Might be worth double-checking with Mira though.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Bo—I’ll mark the community center lobby as the likely spot for now and check with Mira to confirm before I tell anyone else.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Rey, I heard you’re pulling together the repair drive—want me to bring over my toolbox and a couple spare extension cords?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That’d be really helpful, Gus—thank you. If you can bring them by the morning of, I’ll make sure there’s a spot set aside for you.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Perfect, I’ll bring the toolbox and extension cords by that morning, and I’ll stick around in case anyone needs an extra hand.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’m glad we’re doing the repair drive, but I’m already worried about where everyone will park and how we’ll keep the drop-off line from blocking the street.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Are we sure we’ve got permission to use the lot by the pharmacy, or is that just something people are assuming?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That’s exactly what I’m worried about—we shouldn’t advertise it until someone confirms with the pharmacy in writing. I can ask, but I’d rather not be the only one handling the logistics.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Mara, I was thinking the repair drive could be a great chance to bring a few different neighbor groups together—how are you feeling about the planning so far?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: I’m feeling hopeful about it, Jules—bringing the groups together feels exactly right. I’d like us to make sure everyone has a clear role so it feels welcoming, not chaotic.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That makes sense—I can reach out to a few folks from each group and ask what they’d feel comfortable handling, then we can match people to roles before the day arrives.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Hey Dane, I’m starting a list for the repair drive—do you know what supplies folks need most right now?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I’m a bit late to the details as usual, but I can ask around today. My guess is tarps, basic tools, and cleaning supplies, though I’ll confirm before you add too much.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Thanks, Dane—I'll pencil those in as tentative and wait for your confirmations before I put out the full list.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Faye, I was just about to ask if you’d heard who’s bringing tools for the repair drive—I’ve been trying to keep everyone in the loop.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I haven’t heard a firm list yet, Tess, but I can ask around at pickup today and see which parents can bring basics like screwdrivers and pliers.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’d be wonderful, Faye—if you hear who can bring what, I’ll pass the word along so we don’t end up with twelve hammers and no pliers.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Rosa, I only skimmed the notice—what’s the main thing we need for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: The main thing is working small appliances and tools that just need minor fixes—think lamps, fans, toasters, and hand tools. If folks can label what’s wrong with each item, that helps us keep the repair tables moving.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—small stuff with a note on what’s busted. I’ll tell folks not to drag over anything huge or totally dead.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Leo, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—do you need an extra pair of hands with anything?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Yes, thanks—could you help sort tools and check people in at the table?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I can do that. What time should I be there to help set up?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Nell, I’m helping get the word out about the repair drive—want me to swing by later with the details or pass them along now?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Pass them along now if you don’t mind—I’m still catching up on what everyone’s organizing around here.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely—it's a neighborhood repair drive for small household fixes, tools, bikes, and the like; I’ll send you the time and spot, and feel free to bring anything that needs a look.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Hi Eli, I’m starting a list for the repair drive—who’s bringing tools, and where should we have folks drop things off?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Morning, Opal. Let’s use my garage for drop-off Saturday from 9 to noon, and I can bring my basic tool kit and a folding table.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Great, Eli—I’ll mark your garage as the Saturday drop-off spot from 9 to noon, with your basic tool kit and folding table on the list.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Hana, what repairs are we focusing on first, and who’s already signed up to help?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I don’t have the list in front of me yet, so I’d rather confirm before saying for sure. Let me check which repairs were marked urgent and who’s already signed up.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Alright, please check the urgent list first, then tell me what help is still missing.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Oren, I’m just catching up while I’m out—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right, the repair drive—last I heard folks were still gathering broken lamps and small appliances at the community room, though I may be a bit behind on the details.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Thanks, that helps—I'll swing by the community room and see if they need anything else while I'm out.
